title: Cost Control: Token Economics
objective: After this lesson you will be able to account token spend per feature, project monthly costs, apply caching/routing/batching levers in ROI order, and isolate tenants in caches to prevent cross-user leakage.
why: LLM bills scale with success: every user multiplies tokens, and unmeasured spend compounds silently until finance calls. Cost control is accounting first (per-feature spend), then levers in ROI order (cache, route, batch, right-size) — with tenant isolation as a hard constraint, because shared caches across users leak PII with extra steps.

blocks.text: Attribute every token to a feature and tier (input/output, model, retriever): per-1k-task cost = Σ(calls × tokens × price). Dashboards per feature reveal the hogs (usually one: verbose drafts, uncached repeats). Unmeasured spend optimizes nothing — accounting precedes all levers, always.

blocks.caption: Per-task cost × volume × 30: budgets from arithmetic, not anxiety

blocks.text: **Cache** repeats (identical/similar queries — biggest win, lowest risk). **Route** by difficulty (small model for triage, large for edge judgment). **Batch** offline work (nightly digests at bulk rates). **Right-size** models per tier (downgrade where evals hold). Order by savings-per-effort: caching first (days of work, 30–60% cuts typical), re-architecting last. Each lever re-measured on gold — savings that break quality are losses.

blocks.caption: Tenant + class in every key: isolation by construction

blocks.text: Caches keyed without tenant serve Alice's order history to Bob: cross-tenant leakage via performance optimization. Rules: personalized answers keyed per-tenant always; public content shared with version tags; policy content tenant-scoped. Audit cache keys like access-control rules — because they are.

blocks.title: Project the bill
blocks.note: Run it: triage $0.0049/task ($147/mo), draft $0.0185 ($555/mo), total $702/mo at 1k tasks/day. Draft dominates — cache and right-size there first. Budgets direct levers, not hunches.

items: Account per feature/tier first: per-task cost × volume × 30 — unmeasured spend optimizes nothing
Levers in ROI order: cache → route → batch → right-size, each re-measured on gold
Tenant + class in every cache key: personalization never shares; isolation audited like access control

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice projector and name the dominant feature with its share. (b) Apply 50% cache hit-rate to triage (halve its calls) and recompute the total; state savings. (c) Write the cache-key rule for: order status (personal), returns policy (public), ticket draft (personal) — with tenant handling each.
hints: Dominant: draft $555 of $702 (~79%) — levers target drafts first, triage second.
Cached triage: $147 → $73.50; new total $628.50; savings $73.50/mo (~10%). Small lever, measured exactly.
Keys: order status t:{tenant}:... (personal, isolated); policy public:... (shared, versioned); draft t:{tenant}:... (personal).
exercise.why: Dominance analysis (where money goes), lever math (what caching saves), and isolation rules (what shares with whom) are the three cost judgments — each computed, with leakage designed out.
exercise.code: // Cost-lever pattern: project → target dominant → apply → re-measure on gold.

quiz.q: Token bill triples post-launch. First move?
options: Per-feature accounting first — then levers in ROI order on measured hogs
quiz.explain: Unmeasured spend optimizes nothing: account per feature/tier, then cache/route/batch/right-size by savings-per-effort.

quiz.q: Global answer cache across users including order data. Risk?
options: Cross-tenant PII leakage: personalized answers served across users — tenant + class in every key
quiz.explain: Cache keys are access-control rules: personal data never shares keys across tenants. Isolation by construction, audited like permissions.

quiz.q: Caching cuts 40% of calls but gold hit-rate drops. Verdict?
options: Loss: savings that break quality are losses — re-measure every lever on gold before keeping
quiz.explain: Levers re-measured on gold, always. Stale-cache misses are quality regressions wearing savings costumes.

summary: Account per feature, lever in ROI order with gold re-measurement, isolate tenants in every key. Money managed like latency: measured, budgeted, owned.
